description.body: Slender, yellow or brown, two pairs of narrow, fringed wings
description.mouthparts: Asymmetrical; used to scrape leaf surfaces and extract fluids

damage.direct_feeding: Piercing of plant cells and sucking of cell contents, leaving bleached or silvery flecks or patches that can turn brown and necrotic. Causes leaf and flower distortion and stunting. Small black faecal flecks visible within damaged areas.

feeding_preferences.Western flower thrips: Leaves and flowers; flowers/flower buds preferred
feeding_preferences.Japanese flower thrips: Leaves primarily; can occur in flowers

damage.secondary_effects: Damage can predispose plants to Botrytis infection.

virus_transmission.mechanism: First instar larvae acquire virus from infected plants; adults transmit virus during feeding. Adults remain infective for life.

symptoms_of_virus_infection: Leaf distortion, bronzing, yellowing, and necrosis

regulatory_status.TSWV: Regulated Non-Quarantine Pest (RNQP) in Begonia x hiemalis, Capsicum annuum, Chrysanthemum, Gerbera, Impatiens, Pelargonium
regulatory_status.INSV: Regulated Non-Quarantine Pest (RNQP) in Begonia x hiemalis

life_cycle.reproduction: Can reproduce asexually; multiple generations per growing season
life_cycle.notes: Indoor-grown plants more vulnerable due to fewer natural enemies

cultural: Monitor plants regularly for early signs of thrips
Remove and destroy heavily infested plant parts
Maintain healthy populations of natural enemies
chemical: Use insecticides judiciously; follow local guidelines and label instructions
management.integrated: Combine monitoring, cultural control, natural predators, and targeted insecticide use

references: UK Ornamental Crop Guides: Thrips control in protected ornamental crops
Colorado State University Extension, Pest Notes: Thrips in Vegetables and Ornamentals
